Every size and capability claim carries a citation.

args.objective: Recommend a concrete, current stack for building a lightweight, realistic, fully-offline Urdu text-to-speech that runs on-device on Android and iOS, built by fine-tuning an existing Urdu-capable pretrained model (not training from scratch). The output drives an architecture decision, so it must name specific models, runtimes, datasets, and a phonemization path — not a survey.
args.done_when: You return a report that answers all of the following, each backed by a current source/link (2024–2026 preferred): (1) A recommended base model to fine-tune, with its license, approximate parameter count / on-disk size, and a one-paragraph reason it beats the alternatives for lightweight on-device Urdu. Compare at least: Piper/rhasspy (VITS), Meta MMS-TTS 'urd', Coqui VITS, and one modern option (StyleTTS2 or similar) — say why each is in or out for MOBILE OFFLINE use. (2) The on-device runtime to actually ship inference on both Android and iOS offline — check sherpa-onnx and onnxruntime-mobile specifically: confirm from current docs whether each supports VITS/Piper-style TTS on Android AND iOS, and note expected model size + rough latency on a mid-range phone. (3) At least two Urdu speech datasets usable for fine-tuning (e.g. Mozilla Common Voice Urdu, OpenSLR Urdu, any single-speaker Urdu corpora), each with approximate hours, number/gender of speakers, sample-rate/quality, and license. (4) The Urdu text→phoneme path: does espeak-ng support Urdu ('ur') and is it good enough, and what are the known hard problems for Urdu specifically (diacritics/aerab often absent in written text, Nastaliq, numerals, code-switching with English). (5) A clear licensing flag: for every model and dataset named, state whether it permits commercial use or is non-commercial/restricted.
args.decide_yourself: Which additional candidates are worth comparing; how deep to go on each; how to structure the report; whether to recommend a single stack or present a primary + fallback when the evidence is genuinely split.
args.context: Project is a cold/empty repo at UrduTTS. User decisions already fixed: target = on-device mobile (Android + iOS), fully offline; approach = fine-tune a pretrained Urdu-capable model, NOT from scratch; must be lightweight AND realistic (these pull against each other on a phone). Commercial vs non-commercial intent is UNKNOWN, so licensing must be explicit for everything you name. Key names to investigate: Piper (rhasspy/piper), Meta MMS-TTS (facebook/mms-tts-urd), Coqui TTS / XTTS, StyleTTS2, sherpa-onnx (k2-fsa), onnxruntime-mobile, espeak-ng Urdu support, Mozilla Common Voice Urdu, OpenSLR (search for Urdu/Crowdsourced South Asian corpora).
args.boundaries: Do not write code. Repository is read-only for you. Keep the focus on MOBILE OFFLINE deployment — discard options that only realistically run server-side unless they can be distilled/exported to a mobile runtime, and say so. Explicitly flag any non-commercial or research-only license (MMS-TTS in particular is believed to be CC-BY-NC — verify).
args.budget: One focused research pass. If the base-model choice is clear-cut, say so and don't pad with weaker alternatives. Stop and report rather than chase exhaustive benchmarks.
args.deliver: Standard report plus a short "recommended stack" block: base model → runtime → dataset(s) → phonemizer, each on one line with its license, so it can be pasted into a decision record.
